decisions.reason: The secure document storage is a feature of the super-app ecosystem the firm publicly champions, so it costs little to keep and supports the announced platform direction even though it is only briefly mentioned.

The identity-bound wallet ties the firm's core identity expertise to payments, which is central to its super-app story, so management would attribute weak early traction to market ramp-up rather than drop it.

The NFC tag authenticator is the most peripheral, hardware-dependent offering and is only mentioned, but it builds on the firm's authentication heritage and was just launched, so management would likely persist for now.
The payment and wallet framework has its own page and anchors the payments pillar of the announced platform strategy, so visible commitment and sunk investment strongly favour keeping it.
The multi-service mobile app platform is the core of the firm's announced super-app direction, so dropping it would contradict the strategy management must justify.
The application shielding library has its own page, rests on the firm's decades of patented app-security expertise, and likely brings steady licensing revenue, so it remains a committed offering.
